paragraphs: Here's the lesson I love, friend. Seven years of work for Rachel "seemed but a few days because of his love for her" (Genesis 29:20). The years I spent stuck in a junk drawer never felt like a few days, I promise you. Whatever you're working toward, what you love changes how long the wait feels.

But a long, faithful wait can still end in a morning you never saw coming. After seven years, Jacob wakes up and "there was Leah!" (Genesis 29:25). I'm not joking about this one, because I think it hurt everybody in that house. Laban only brought up his custom after the work was done (Genesis 29:26), so read the terms BEFORE you start baking.

Then Jacob agrees to seven more years, and we're told he "loved Rachel more than Leah" (Genesis 29:30). I think Leah felt that, but that's me guessing, friend. Love can carry you through a lot, and it still needs honest hands around it. Hang on to that, because this family's story is not over.
